# Workflow Conventions

## CI/release workflow separation

CI (build/test) and release (publish/tag) are separate workflows:

- **`placeframe-ci.yml`**: Triggers on `push: [dev]` and `pull_request: [dev]`. Contains: preflight, build-docker, publish-compose, ensure-release-pr. The `ensure-release-pr` job is gated on all builds passing and only runs on dev push. No Unity job — the repo's last Unity app (Map Registration Tool) was deleted and the capture tier's builds live in placeframe-capture-tool; the shared `unity-build.yml` continues to live in the [unity-devkit](https://github.com/outernet-foundation/unity-devkit) repo for repos that need it.
- **`placeframe-release.yml`**: Triggers on `push: [main]`, `workflow_dispatch`, and on the Placeframe workflow completing green on `dev` (`workflow_run`). The `publish-stable` job (main pushes + non-dev dispatch) reuses CI artifacts by looking up the successful CI run for the same SHA via `gh api`. The `publish-dev` job (green dev pushes, or a dispatch with `dev-publish=true` + `dev-run-id` against `dev`) runs pubpkg's `publish-dev`: immutable `-dev.<ci-run-id>` prereleases of every path-diff-changed package, keyed by the CI run that proved greenness — no git tags, npm `latest` untouched, and the printed versions are the consumption interface (exact pins by hand). Dispatch matters because `workflow_run` triggers only register from the workflow file on the **default branch**: until the release merge lands this file on `main`, the dev channel is armed solely by dispatching against `dev` (a dispatch runs the dispatched ref's copy of the file). The dev jobs live in this workflow file — not in placeframe-ci — because npm allows one trusted publisher per package, bound to a single workflow filename that must be shared with the stable publish jobs. PyPI packages are split out of both flows into per-package matrix jobs (`publish-stable-pypi`, `publish-dev-pypi`), each entry under its own `pypi-<project>` GitHub environment: PyPI trusted publishers are identified by `(owner, repo, workflow filename, environment)` with one project per tuple, so multi-package repos need one environment per PyPI package. The main jobs exclude the PyPI pair; the matrix runs before `publish-stable` so `create-release` sees every tag. Uses `cancel-in-progress: false` — never abort a publish mid-flight, and the shared `release` concurrency group serializes dev publishes against stable releases.
- All workflow logic lives in Python scripts invoked via `uv run` — no inline shell conditionals or loops (per repo-root convention).
